name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
bio: The site where the Treaty of Waitangi was signed in 1840, with the Treaty House, a carved meeting house and a giant war canoe.

name: Piercy Island
bio: The island with the Hole in the Rock, a natural arch large enough for cruise boats to pass through.

name: Russell
bio: The country's first capital, a waterfront village of colonial buildings, including Pompallier Mission and Christ Church.

name: Paihia
bio: The main tourist base on the bay, a beachfront town with cruise and ferry departures.

name: Haruru Falls
bio: A horseshoe-shaped waterfall on the Waitangi River, reached by a short path from Paihia.

name: Urupukapuka Island
bio: The bay's biggest island, with walking tracks, quiet beaches and views of the surrounding islands.

name: Hundertwasser Toilets
bio: A colourful public toilet designed by Friedensreich Hundertwasser, a quirky landmark in Kawakawa.

name: Hundertwasser Art Centre
bio: A colourful, grass-roofed building with a gold dome, designed by Hundertwasser and housing a Māori art gallery.

name: Whangarei Falls
bio: A 26-metre waterfall dropping into a pool, with a short loop track and a viewing platform.

name: Poor Knights Islands
bio: A marine reserve of volcanic islands with sea caves and arches, rated among the world's best dive sites.

name: Tutukaka
bio: A small marina village on the coast, the departure point for Poor Knights Islands dive and cruise trips.

name: Mount Manaia
bio: A steep volcanic peak above Whangārei Heads, with a rewarding scramble to a view over the harbour.

name: Claphams Clocks
bio: A museum of more than 1,500 clocks and watches at the Town Basin.

name: Cape Reinga Lighthouse
bio: A white lighthouse on the north-western tip, with signposts to cities around the world and views of the meeting seas.

name: Te Paki Sand Dunes
bio: Giant white dunes that visitors sandboard down, a short drive from Cape Reinga.

name: Ninety Mile Beach
bio: A 88-km stretch of flat white sand along the west coast, used as a road at low tide by tours and 4WD vehicles.

name: Spirits Bay
bio: A remote bay of golden sand where, in Māori tradition, spirits begin their journey to the afterlife.

name: Tapotupotu Bay
bio: A sheltered bay with a campground and swimming, at the end of the Cape Reinga coastal walk.

name: Tāne Mahuta
bio: The largest known living kauri tree, about 2,000 years old and over 50 metres tall.

name: Te Matua Ngāhere
bio: Father of the Forest, a huge kauri with the widest girth in the country, reached by a short bush walk.

name: Four Sisters
bio: A cluster of four kauri trees joined at the base, beside the road through the forest.

name: Hokianga Harbour
bio: A long, tidal harbour with huge white sand dunes on the north head, reached by ferry or boat.

name: Opononi
bio: A harbourside village famous for Opo the friendly dolphin of the 1950s, with views over the dunes.

name: Kauri Museum
bio: A museum of kauri gum, timber and the pioneer industries that shaped Northland, at Matakohe.
